items.title: 同一LLMに異なる専門医のペルソナを与え、議論途中で必要な専門家を追加すると、医学QAの精度は改善するか？
items.summary:
同一LLMに異なる専門医のペルソナを与え、議論途中で必要な専門家を追加すると、医学QAの精度は改善するか？

→結論：医学国家試験形式のMedQAでは精度が改善。ただし、実臨床での有効性は未検証。

EMNLP 2025 Main（被引用数：5件、Scholar Feed掲載値）

背景

UAEのMBZUAI、中国電子科技大学、スイスのEPFLによる研究。

従来の医療Multi-Agentでは、最初に専門家の構成を決めるため、議論途中で新たに必要となった専門知識を補いにくい。

方法

GPT-4.1-miniを共通の基盤モデルとし、異なる専門医のペルソナを付与。
最初は1人の専門家LLMから開始。
議論途中でLLM自身がKnowledge Gap（専門知識の不足）をYes/Noで判定。
知識不足があれば、その分野の専門家ペルソナを持つLLMを追加して議論を継続。
最大3ラウンド議論し、Moderator LLMが最終回答。
医学国家試験形式のMedQAで評価。

結果

MedQA：単一LLM＋CoT 84.21% → KAMAC 88.14%（+3.93ポイント）。
専門家を固定する従来手法に対し、議論途中で専門家を追加できる仕組みを実現。

限界

専門家は同一LLMに異なるペルソナを与えたもので、独立した医学知識を持つモデルではない。
精度改善がペルソナ、複数回推論、動的な専門家追加のどれに由来するかは十分に切り分けられていない。
Knowledge Gapの検出精度や実臨床での有効性は十分に検証されていない。

タイトル

A Knowledge-driven Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Enhancing Medical Decision-making

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」、と明言しています。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

专利权人铃木工业株式会社被看似利害关系人的德电株式会社起诉（异议编号：2017-700867），但专利权人在专利局赢得了专利。

此外，德电株式会社另行提起无效宣告审判（审判号2022-800026），同样以专利权人胜诉而告终。

德电株式会社就此向知识产权高等法院提起上诉。

在知识产权高等法院中，“专利第6114435号的权利要求中，在日本特许厅于2020年8月17日作出的关于无效宣告案件第2022号的审判决定中，审判请求不成立的部分中” -800026，1、4至6已被撤销，部分专利权被撤销。

此外，“一审判决认定发明1、4至6具有创造性的判断是错误的，原告主张的撤销审判决定的理由之一是发明1不具备创造性，以及发明不具备创造性”。

发明4具有创造性。

经判定，发明不具有创造性，发明5不具有创造性，发明6不具有创造性。

因此，[权利要求2]和[权利要求3]的专利权似乎仍然存在。

我们回顾一下专利局的审查阶段。

专利局审查员（Mitsuharu Miyazaki）向申请人提交了五篇引用文献和参考专利文献，其中包括JP-A-05-198370。

另一方面，在知识产权高等法院，申请人在无效审判中提出了五个案件（附件A第1号：美国重新颁发的专利发明说明书第36787号）（2022-800026~附件A5）。

被提出。 然后，对于这些证据A1至A5，决定“取消与专利第6114435号的权利要求1和4至6相关的部分”。

为什么专利局审查员（Mitsuharu Miyazaki）找不到证据A1至A5？ 专利局审查员的研究能力再次被证明是薄弱的。

此外，在异议审判中，异议人提出了包括证据A第1号：日本专利申请公开第2009-272295号在内的四个案例，但专利局审查员（田村义明等人）“与权利要求有关的专利”维持1至6条”，与知识产权高等法院的判决不同。

专利局审查阶段仅凭审查员的草率检索而授予专利是不可接受的。

此外，基于专利局审理中的错误决定而维持专利权也是不可接受的。

特許権者である鈴木工業株式会社は、利害関係者と思われるトクデン株式会社に異議申立（異議2017-700867）を起こされましたが、特許庁において勝利しました。

また、トクデン株式会社は別途、無効審判（審判2022-800026）を起こしましたがこれも又、特許権者の勝利に終わっています。

トクデン株式会社はこれを不服として知的財産高等裁判所に訴えました。

知的財産高等裁判所においては、「特許庁が無効２０２２－８０００２６号事件について令和５年８月１７日にした審決において審判の請求は成り立たないとした部分のうち、特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」され、特許権の一部が取り消されました。

更に、「本件発明１及び４から６までについて進歩性を認めた審決の判断は誤りであり、原告の主張する本件審決の取消事由のうち、本件発明１に係る進歩性欠如、本件発明４に係る進歩性欠如、本件5 発明５に係る進歩性欠如及び本件発明６に係る進歩性欠如は認められると判断する。」としています。

その結果、特許権は【請求項２】と【請求項３】とが残ったようです。

ここで特許庁における審査段階を振り返ってみます。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、特開平０５－１９８３７０号公報を含めて５件の引用文献と参考特許文献を出願人に提示しています。

一方、知的財産高等裁判所においては、無効審判（2022-800026）で審判請求人より提示された（甲第１号証：米国再発行特許発明第３６７８７号明細書）を含む５件（甲１号証〜甲５号証）が提示されています。

そして、これら甲１号証〜甲５号証をもって、「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」とされました。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、何故これら甲１号証〜甲５号証を見つけることができなかったのでしょうか。

ここでも、特許庁の審査官の調査能力が弱いことが証明されています。

更に、異議審判においては、甲第１号証：特開２００９－２７２２９５号公報を含む４件が異議申立人より提示されていますが、特許庁の審判官（田村嘉章ら）は「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１ないし６に係る特許を維持する。」として、知的財産高等裁判所の判断とは異なる結論をしています。

特許庁の審査段階における審査官のいい加減な（サーチ）に基づいた、特許付与は許されません。

更には、特許庁の審判においても誤った判断により特許権の維持を行なったのも、これまた許されません。

従って、本来なら、鈴木工業株式会社の出願に対して、特許庁は特許を与えるべきでなかった、と考えます。

items.title: Jensen Huang says engineers should burn $250,000 of AI a year, and Apple just cut its engineers' AI budget to about $50,
items.summary:
Jensen Huang says engineers should burn $250,000 of AI a year, and Apple just cut its engineers' AI budget to about $50,000.

And Apple plans to cut it again.

Last month, some Apple engineers saw their daily AI spending cap drop from $300 to $200, Bloomberg reported. Some engineering teams could be cut to $100 a day next. Many groups outside engineering already sit at $100, and Apple has considered going as low as $25 for some of them.

In March, Jensen said on the All-In podcast that he'd be deeply alarmed if a $500,000 engineer used less than $250,000 of AI tokens in a year. He also said Dario Amodei's forecast of hundreds of billions in AI revenue was too conservative.

So Jensen's rule is simple: AI spending should run about half of what an engineer gets paid.

By my math, at about 250 workdays a year, $200 a day comes to roughly $50,000. The planned $100 cap comes to roughly $25,000.

By Jensen's rule, a $100 daily cap only makes sense for an engineer paid about $50,000 a year.

And Apple still wants its people using MORE AI. It's steering teams toward cheaper models and AI that runs on the device, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has said Apple's internal work runs heavily on Anthropic's models.

I think Apple just showed where the real limit on the AI boom sits now: The finance department.

And that's just ONE company:

- Accenture capped Claude at $29 a month per employee on October 1, after some staff had been spending up to $1,000 a month, 404 Media reported.
- Uber burned through its entire 2026 AI budget in about 4 months, then capped AI coding tools at $1,500 a month per tool.
- Microsoft has cut allowances too, and its AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told Bloomberg that Anthropic is extremely expensive and that Microsoft wants to eventually get rid of that cost.
- Meta had internal leaderboards ranking staff by how many tokens they used, and now it has introduced token budgets.

The usage is clearly there. Uber's engineers used the tools so much they spent a full year's budget in 4 months.

So the people saying stop are the ones paying the bill.

That's a huge problem for the AI labs, for one reason: Their spending is already locked in. 

Anthropic has committed to $895 billion, mostly for computing power. OpenAI has signed more than $1.4 trillion of compute deals. And paying for all of it depends on companies spending more on AI per worker every year.

Apple, Accenture, Uber and Microsoft all pay for Anthropic's models, and Anthropic could start its IPO roadshow as early as next week. Its own filing shows revenue grew about 47% from the second quarter to the third, down from about 144% the quarter before, and price cuts took about $600 million out of revenue.

Plenty of people will say this is just housekeeping, and they have numbers:

Bloomberg says few Apple engineers ever used the full $300, so the savings may be small. Cheaper models can do the same work for less. Apple's R&D still rose 32% to $45.8 billion in fiscal 2026, partly because of AI. And more companies start using AI every month, so total spending can keep growing even with a cap on each worker.

But Jensen's pitch depends on spending per worker going UP. Apple, Microsoft, Meta, Uber and Accenture are all writing rules that push it down.

So the first question for Anthropic's roadshow should be simple: How much are its biggest customers spending per employee compared with a year ago, and how many of them have put caps in place?

Who's right about what an engineer's AI is worth, Jensen Huang or Apple's finance team?

Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu tự động, được thiết kế để giúp bạn tìm kiếm thông tin, tổng hợp nội dung và thực hiện các tác vụ liên quan đến dữ liệu trên internet mà không cần hỏi lại nhiều lần.

**Tôi có thể làm được những việc sau:**

1. **Tìm kiếm và tra cứu thông tin**  
   - Tìm bài viết, tin tức hoặc nội dung trên mạng xã hội (ví dụ: timeline của một tài khoản, tìm kiếm từ khóa trên X/Twitter…).  
   - Tra cứu thông tin chung hoặc tin tức gần đây qua công cụ `lookup`.

2. **Đọc và trích xuất nội dung từ trang web**  
   - Lấy toàn bộ văn bản từ một URL cụ thể bằng công cụ `fetch`.

3. **Tìm và đọc bài báo khoa học**  
   - Tìm kiếm bài báo trên arXiv theo từ khóa.  
   - Lấy nội dung text của một bài báo (mặc định 5 trang đầu, tối đa 8.000 ký tự).

4. **Trình bày và định dạng dữ liệu**  
   - Chuyển danh sách các mục (tiêu đề, URL, tóm tắt…) thành văn bản theo nhiều mẫu: `brief`, `sections`, `bullets`, `thread`, `daily_ai_vn`.

5. **Gửi nội dung đi**  
   - Gửi một đoạn văn bản đến người nhận (cần bạn xác nhận bằng cờ `confirmed` nếu muốn thực hiện ngay).

6. **Tìm kiếm trong tài liệu nội bộ**  
   - Tra cứu chính sách hoặc hướng dẫn sử dụng trong kho tài liệu nội bộ (`policy`).

**Cách tôi làm việc:**  
Nếu yêu cầu của bạn thiếu thông tin hoặc không rõ ràng, tôi sẽ tự đặt giả thiết hợp lý và gọi công cụ ngay lập tức thay vì hỏi lại bạn. Khi bạn yêu cầu gửi, đăng hoặc xuất bản nội dung, tôi sẽ thực hiện luôn để bạn không phải chờ đợi.

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.
